title: Drop and Border
premise: Sable Blackwood, a burned-out private security contractor, receives a calendar invite from his dead handler, Marcus Vane, scheduling a meeting for the next morning — and when he arrives, he's ambushed by rival contractors who believe Vane left him a ledger exposing a private intelligence network that launders justice for the wealthy. The 'inheritance' Vane actually left him is a dead-man's-switch key and a name: Sable's own, listed as an asset he never knew he was. To survive, Sable must trade the one secret worth killing for — proof that the incident that broke his sleep was ordered, not accidental — while deciding whether to hand it to the law, the network, or burn it. In the end he gives the truth to the victims' families instead of any institution, dismantles the network's local cell at terrible cost, and finally sleeps through the night.
about_author: Lena Thornbury is a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments before turning to fiction about the people inside them. She lives off-grid on the Atlantic coast, where she claims her best plot twists arrive during storms.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Sable Blackwood, running on four hours' sleep, guards a paranoid client through a tense night while flashbacks of 'the incident' gnaw at him. At dawn his phone chimes: a meeting invitation from Marcus Vane, his handler — dead eleven days. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into disbelief.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Calendar
chapters.summary: Sable investigates: the invite came from Vane's verified account, scheduled before his death. He visits the morgue records and finds the body cremated against protocol. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion that nothing about Vane's death is what it seems.

chapters.title: Room 404
chapters.summary: Sable keeps the meeting at a dockside hotel. Instead of Vane, he finds three rival contractors waiting — and a fourth corpse in the bathtub wearing Vane's watch. They want the inheritance they're sure Vane left him. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: Terms of Extraction
chapters.summary: Sable talks his way out by bluffing knowledge of a ledger, then goes dark in a safehouse. He discovers Vane's real bequest: a dead-man's-switch key and a single typed word — his own surname. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: cold fear; he isn't just a courier, he's cargo.

chapters.title: The Network That Buys Verdicts
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: five years earlier, young contractor Sable takes orders from Vane without questions, including one operation in Rellwick that went wrong. POV: Sable (past). Emotional beat: complicity — the reader sees the incident forming.

chapters.title: Hollow Point Hospitality
chapters.summary: The rivals find the safehouse. Sable escapes through a storm drain after a brutal close-quarters fight, wounded, losing his go-bag but keeping the key taped to his ribs. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: survival instinct overriding exhaustion.

chapters.title: Ines
chapters.summary: Sable seeks out Ines Okafor, a disgraced forensic accountant and Vane's former lover, who confirms the ledger exists: names, payments, verdicts bought across three countries. She warns him the switch expires in nine days. POV: alternating Sable/Ines. Emotional beat: wary alliance, first spark of trust.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says About Me
chapters.summary: Ines decrypts a fragment: Sable's name appears as an active asset, recruited years ago without his knowledge — his security firm was always a network front. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: identity collapse; his whole career was someone else's design.

chapters.title: The Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: Sable's current client, shipping magnate Aldous Renner, reveals himself as a network board member and offers Sable a choice: deliver the key and be rich, or be listed as a liability. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: A countdown structure: Sable and Ines trace the switch's server to a data center in Rotterdam while dodging surveillance. They learn the full release would also expose dozens of innocents Vane used as cover. POV: Sable/Ines. Emotional beat: the cost of justice coming into focus.

chapters.title: Rellwick Revisited
chapters.summary: Sable returns to Rellwick, site of the incident, and meets Mara Voss, whose brother died there. She has spent years pulling threads and recognizes the operation's signature. POV: Sable/Mara. Emotional beat: shame meeting grief; a witness he can't lie to.

chapters.title: Vane's Voice
chapters.summary: A hidden message from Vane plays: he faked his death, apologizes for using Sable, and explains the switch can't distinguish guilty from innocent — only Sable can decide what to release. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: betrayal and forgiveness tangled together.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Archive
chapters.summary: Renner's team hits Ines's archive; she's taken, and the fragment copies are seized. Sable escapes with only the physical key. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: rage — the trade he refused to make has been made for him.

chapters.title: The Market for Secrets
chapters.summary: Sable infiltrates a network auction where stolen dossiers are sold, locating Ines and learning Renner plans to trigger the switch remotely and blame Sable for the fallout. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: clarity — he has six days and no allies left but the ones he chooses.

chapters.title: Mara's Terms
chapters.summary: Mara agrees to help, but on her terms: the families hear everything first, before any court or journalist. Sable, who once traded secrets for pay, accepts a deal he can't profit from. POV: Sable/Mara. Emotional beat: justice redefined outside the law.

chapters.title: Rotterdam
chapters.summary: Sable breaches the data center during a blackout, frees Ines from a holding room, and physically seizes the switch core as alarms cascade. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: adrenaline cresting into resolve.

chapters.title: Renner's Offer, Again
chapters.summary: Cornered on the roof, Renner makes his final offer — wealth, erasure, a new name — and reveals the incident in Rellwick was ordered to test Sable's loyalty. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: the wound named at last; grief becomes weapon.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Climax part one: Sable publicly trades the one secret worth killing for — the Rellwick order, with Renner's signature — giving it not to police or press but to the victims' families simultaneously, making it unbuyable. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: catharsis through surrender.

chapters.title: Everything Burns Differently
chapters.summary: Climax part two: Renner's men storm the family meeting; Sable, Ines, and Mara hold them off until the released evidence triggers arrests mid-assault. Renner, exposed, tries to destroy the core and is stopped. POV: rotating trio. Emotional beat: chaos resolving into accountability.

chapters.title: Aftermath Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Weeks later: hearings begin, the network fractures, and Sable refuses reinstatement anywhere official. Ines rebuilds her life; Mara files the last of her brother's paperwork. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning, debts partially paid.

chapters.title: Sleep Through the Night
chapters.summary: Sable closes his firm, returns Vane's watch to the sea off Rellwick, and — for the first time since the incident — sleeps until morning. A final line hints another invitation may someday arrive. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: belonging found in chosen loyalties, rest finally earned.

chapters.title: Epilogue: The Next Handler
chapters.summary: Short coda from an unnamed new handler opening a file labeled BLACKWOOD, S. — STATUS: UNAVAILABLE — and closing it with something like respect. POV: unknown. Emotional beat: ominous serenity; the world turns, but Sable is done being its instrument.
